project.objective: Who were the parents of Mauro Cruz Corona, born about 1910 in or near Nueva Italia, Michoacán, Mexico, and what were his exact birth date and place?

questions.question: What were the exact birth date and place of Mauro Cruz Corona, born about 1910 in or near Nueva Italia, Michoacán, Mexico?
questions.rationale: The tree records only 'about 1910, near Nueva Italia, Michoacán' — an approximate, unsourced starting point. Mexican civil registro records (and parish registers for earlier decades) routinely capture the precise date, the specific locality, and both parents' names in a single entry. Resolving the birth record is the highest-leverage first step: it will simultaneously fix the birth fact and provide the most direct path to parentage. The siblings' birth places in Guerrero towns (La Unión and Coahuayutla municipalities, 1913–1918) suggest the family was mobile; the birth place itself may differ from Nueva Italia and is currently unverified.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: The 1910 Guerrero Civil Birth Registration (src_002, a_079, a_080) is an original record with primary information: the father Sóstenes Cruz appeared in person before the civil registrar 14 days after the birth and stated the date (22 November 1910) and place (La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero). The 1930 Mexico National Census (src_001, a_034) independently corroborates birth state Guerrero from a different institutional source and informant. Michoacán indexed civil registro (collection 1916243, three searches) and Michoacán indexed Catholic church records (collection 1883388) were both negative — the Apatzingán area is not indexed in those collections, but the Guerrero civil registration superseded the need for Michoacán browse fallbacks. The single conflict (c_001: birth year ~1914 from census vs. 1910 from civil registration) was resolved in favor of the civil registration on the strength of informant proximity and record purpose. The Guerrero Catholic Church Records (collection 1823323) were not searched: a baptism for this event would have been reported by the same informants (the parents) and cannot supply a truly independent corroborating source under the evidence-independence rule; it also cannot plausibly contradict the date or place already established by the original, primary-quality, contemporaneous civil registration. Overturn risk is low. Note: the wiki_read call for Guerrero_Civil_Registration timed out; the registration start date is unverified by the wiki, but the existence of the 1910 registration itself (and the 1908 sibling registration in the same civil system) is self-evidencing that civil registration was operative in Guerrero by at least 1908.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Met. The 1910 Guerrero civil birth registration answers both components of q_001 with precision: exact birth date 22 November 1910 (a_079) and exact birth place La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero, Mexico (a_080). The father presented in person 14 days after the birth — a convincing, contemporaneous answer is in hand.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: Met. Michoacán indexed civil registro (collection 1916243, three name-variant searches), Michoacán indexed Catholic church records (collection 1883388), the 1930 Mexico National Census (the only accessible federal census), and the Guerrero indexed civil registration (collection 1918291) were all searched. Browse-only fallbacks for Michoacán (pli_005, pli_006) were appropriately skipped once the Guerrero birth record was found. The Guerrero Catholic church records (collection 1823323) were not searched — see overturn_risk for the reasoning.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Met. The Guerrero civil birth registration was accessed as an original record via record_read (log_007); the index entry (log_006) was used only to locate it. The 1930 census image ark was noted (ark:/61903/3:1:S3HT-66R3-LH4). No derivative-only reliance.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Met. Two independent sources are present: (1) the 1910 Guerrero civil birth registration (src_002), informant Sóstenes Cruz (father), created contemporaneously by the civil registrar; and (2) the 1930 Mexico National Census (src_001), informant unknown household member, 20 years later, different government system and jurisdiction. They differ in informant, date, institutional origin, and geographic provenance — they are independent. The census corroborates birth state Guerrero independently of the civil registration.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Met. The 1910 Guerrero civil birth registration (a_079, a_080) is an original record with primary information: the father, a direct witness, reported the birth date and place to a civil registrar 14 days after the event. This is the strongest available evidence class for a birth fact.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Met. One conflict existed — c_001, birth year ~1914 (census) vs. 22 November 1910 (civil registration). Resolved (status: resolved) in favor of the civil registration (a_079) on grounds of informant proximity (father vs. unknown household member 20 years later), record purpose (civil registration's explicit purpose was to document the birth date), and well-documented Mexican census age-rounding patterns. No other conflicts are open on q_001.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low — met. The one unsearched named collection is Guerrero Catholic Church Records (collection 1823323, 1576-1979). A baptismal record for this event would have been reported by the same informants as the civil registration (the parents), so it would not constitute a truly independent source under the evidence-independence rule. More critically, a baptismal entry cannot plausibly name a different birth date or place than what is already established by a primary-quality, contemporaneous civil registration made 14 days after birth. No competing evidence, no anomaly in the record, and no FAN research hint suggests a different date or place. Note: the Guerrero Civil Registration wiki page was unavailable (connection timeout); the civil registration start date is unverified by the wiki. However, the self-evident existence of the 1910 civil birth registration and the 1908 sibling registration in the same Guerrero civil system confirms civil registration was operative in this jurisdiction before the target event. The baptism is not a decisive record that gates this declaration.

questions.question: Who were the parents of Mauro Cruz Corona, born about 1910 in or near Nueva Italia, Michoacán, Mexico?
questions.rationale: Parentage is the central objective. The tree carries no parent links for Mauro and no sources. His compound surname 'Cruz Corona' suggests a paternal 'Cruz' line and a maternal 'Corona' line (following Spanish naming conventions), but this is unverified. The birth record sought in q_001 is the most direct evidence and will likely name both parents; civil registro de nacimiento entries in Michoacán typically record father's full name and mother's full name. If q_001 does not resolve parentage, secondary paths include the 1930 census household (siblings Miguel, Liborio, and Facundo Cruz are present in Nueva Italia), church baptismal records from parishes serving the Guerrero municipalities where the siblings were born, and any surviving padrones or civil records from Parácuaro.

items.rationale: FamilySearch collection 1916243 (Mexico, Michoacán, Civil Registration, 1859-1940) is indexed with 8.7 M persons and covers Apatzingán births, marriages, and deaths 1859–1940. A Michoacán registro de nacimiento for ca. 1910 names the child's birth date, time, and place; the father's full name; the mother's full name (maiden surname); and both sets of grandparents. This record could simultaneously answer q_001 (birth date/place) and q_002 (parentage). Search under Cruz and variant de la Cruz, birth year 1908–1912, place Apatzingán. Nueva Italia de Ruiz was within Apatzingán municipality in 1910 — Múgica municipality was not created until 1942.

FamilySearch collection 1883388 (Mexico, Michoacán, Catholic Church Records, 1555-1996) is indexed with 35 M persons and includes bautismos from Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, Apatzingán — the only parish serving the Nueva Italia area in 1905–1920. Searched in parallel with the civil registro because compliance with civil registration was uneven in newly-settled rural areas; the family may have a baptism without a civil registration. A baptismal entry names the infant, baptism date, parents, and often godparents and grandparents.

FamilySearch collection 1307314 (Mexico Census, 1930) is the only federal Mexican census whose household schedules are publicly accessible online. Mauro Cruz Corona (born ca. 1910) would be approximately 20 in 1930. If he remained in the Apatzingán area, this census will show his age, birthplace, and household composition, corroborating or correcting the birth estimate and possibly naming parents. The 1910 and 1921 household schedules are not publicly available online.

FAN/siblings item. Three siblings — Miguel Cruz, Liborio Cruz, and Facundo Cruz — were born in Guerrero municipalities (La Unión and Coahuayutla) ca. 1913–1918. FamilySearch collection 1918291 (Mexico, Guerrero, Civil Registration, 1860-1996) is indexed. Each sibling's birth record names the same father (Cruz) and mother (Corona) as Mauro's, potentially supplying the parents' given names and full compound surnames. This covers the possibility that Mauro's own Michoacán birth record is absent due to Revolutionary disruption, and that the parents' marriage record is in Guerrero.

Browse-only fallback for pli_001. FamilySearch Catalog 190084 (Registros civiles del municipio de Apatzingán, 1867-1930) contains images of the original Apatzingán civil registro not fully captured in the indexed collection 1916243. If the indexed search yields nothing for Mauro Cruz ca. 1910, browse the nacimientos volumes for 1908–1912. No index exists at this level; page-by-page browsing of the birth register is required.

Browse-only fallback for pli_002. FamilySearch Catalog 320208 (Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, Apatzingán, 1866-1967) is the original parish register. If the indexed church search (pli_002) returns nothing, browse the bautismos volumes at the Catalog level for 1908–1912. No name index exists here. The Acahuato parish (Catalog 1107030, 1875–1925) is the nearest secondary parish and should be checked if Apatzingán yields nothing.

items.jurisdiction: La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero, Mexico
items.rationale: GPS parentage questions require a dedicated search for the candidate parents' marriage to each other. Sóstenes Cruz and Apolinar Corona are named as parents on two independent Guerrero civil birth registrations (Mauro's 1910 registration, src_002; Margarito's 1908 registration, src_003). A marriage record for this couple in Guerrero Civil Registration (collection 1918291, personCount 8.4M, fully indexed) would: (1) independently confirm the parentage of Mauro Cruz Corona; (2) supply Sóstenes Cruz's maternal surname (second surname), which is unknown from the birth registrations; and (3) establish Apolinar Corona's maiden name if different from her stated surname. Date window: oldest known child Margarito was born June 1908, so the marriage preceded that date. Apolinar born ~1881 makes a marriage before 1896 unlikely. Search window 1895–1910 covers the most probable range. Search: givenName=Sóstenes, surname=Cruz, spouseGivenName=Apolinar, spouseSurname=Corona, collectionId=1918291, recordType=marriage. Also try the accent-less variant 'Sostenes Cruz'. No Guerrero localities entry (loc_) exists in this project; this item uses the jurisdiction knowledge from loc_001 (which explicitly references collection 1918291 for Guerrero) and the collections_search results obtained this session.

The Montes de Oca judicial district in Guerrero state had active parishes in this period. Search: givenName=Primitivo, surname=Cruz, motherSurname=Corona, collectionId=1918291, birthYearFrom=1906, birthYearTo=1912. Size note: Sóstenes Cruz's maternal surname is unknown; fatherGivenName=Sóstenes may be used as a narrowing filter rather than a required anchor.

log.notes: 28 results returned statewide in collection 1916243 but none from Apatzingán municipality; all from other Michoacán municipalities (Panindícuaro, Maravatío, Zamora, Tacámbaro, etc.); highest matchScore 0.0015, well below the 0.01 threshold; Apatzingán-area records for ca. 1910 may not be fully indexed in this collection.

Statewide Michoacán search adding motherSurname=Corona returned 20 results; all 20 show relativeTerms.mother: absent — no indexed record in collection 1916243 names a Corona mother for Mauro Cruz. Two entries show 'Mauro Cruz' and 'Mauro Crúz' as father in child birth records (QG3Z-J71G for Maria Tomasa Cruz Urbano; QG3Z-DG41 for Susana Crúz Reyes) — these document an adult Mauro Cruz as a father, not his own birth. No birth record for Mauro Cruz Corona found in the indexed Michoacán civil registro. Apatzingán records ca. 1910 appear not indexed in this collection.

de la Cruz variant statewide in collection 1916243: 56 total matches, none from Apatzingán municipality. Top scoring principal birth record is Mauro Cruz born ca. 26 Nov 1913 in Panindícuaro (matchScore 0.0015, wrong place and too late). A death record for a Mauro Cruz born 1908 in Contepec (died 1909) is a different infant. Two entries name 'Mauro Cruz'/'Mauro Crúz' as Father in child birth records (QG3Z-J71G, QG3Z-DG41) — possible later records naming him as a father but not his own birth. Conclusion: Apatzingán birth records for ca. 1910 are not indexed in collection 1916243; the browse-only Catalog 190084 fallback (pli_005) will be needed.

88 total results from collection 1883388 (Michoacán Catholic Church Records) but none from Apatzingán parish. Results are spread across Morelia, Tuxpan, Zinaécuaro, Cojumatlán, Tingüîndín, La Huacana, etc. The Apatzingán parish (Nuestra Señora de la Asunción) bautismos for ca. 1910 are not indexed in this collection — they are browse-only images at Catalog 320208 (pli_006 fallback). No baptism record for Mauro Cruz Corona in the indexed church records layer.

Top match (matchScore 0.042): Mauro Cruz, born 1914 Guerrero, enumerated in Nueva Italia de Ruiz, Múgica, Michoacán in 1930, single. Record read from sidecar reveals household includes all three previously known siblings (Migel/Miguel Cruz b.1916 Guerrero, Libario/Liborio Cruz b.1918 Guerrero, Facundo Cruz b.1920 Guerrero) plus previously unknown older sibling Primitivo Cruz (b.1908 Guerrero). Apolinar Corona (Female, b.1881 Guerrero, surname Corona) co-resident — almost certainly the mother given her Corona surname. Household head is Feliciano Anguiano (b.1903 Michoacán) — an employer/neighbor, not the father. Father not present in this household. All Cruz children born in Guerrero — redirects birth record search to Guerrero civil registro (pli_004). Birth year 1914 differs from estimated ca.1910; the census age is secondary and approximate. imageArk: ark:/61903/3:1:S3HT-66R3-LH4.

Positive: Found Mauro Cruz Corona's own birth registration (ark:/61903/1:1:QGWQ-MCFV, born 22 Nov 1910, La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero) at rank 2, with mother Apolinar Corona confirmed present. Also found siblings Margarito Cruz Corona (b. 1908) and Rufina Cruz Corona (b. 1905/1906), both in Montes de Oca, Guerrero, mother Apolinar Corona. Birth records name both parents — full reads will supply the father's name. Directly answers q_001 (birth date and place).

Mauro Cruz Corona birth record read. Born 22 November 1910, La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero. Registered 6 December 1910, Montes de Oca, Guerrero. Father: Sóstenes Cruz. Mother: Apolinar Corona. Directly answers q_001 (birth date 22 Nov 1910, birth place La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero) and q_002 (parents: Sóstenes Cruz and Apolinar Corona).

Margarito Cruz Corona birth record read. Born 10 June 1908, La Unión, registered 17 June 1908 in Montes de Oca, Guerrero. Father: Sóstenes Cruz. Mother: Apolinar Corona. Corroborates Mauro's birth record: same parents, same locality. Margarito is a previously unknown sibling of Mauro Cruz Corona.

Top hit ark:/61903/1:1:QGWQ-4XR3 is civil marriage of Primitivo Corona & Hilaria Guillen; Sóstenes Cruz listed as Father of Groom with spouse Apolinar Corona — corroborates the couple relationship for q_002 parentage.

No clear match for Primitivo Cruz as principal child born ~1906-1912 with mother surname Corona in Guerrero/La Unión. Top results are 'Primitivo de la Cruz' from other localities or Primitivo Cruz appearing as fathers on later records.

Civil marriage registration of Primitivo Corona and Hilaria Guillen, 24 July 1935, Montes de Oca, Guerrero. Sóstenes Crúz named as Father of Groom; Apolinar Corona named as mother (couple relationship). Third independent document corroborating the Sóstenes Cruz / Apolinar Corona couple for q_002.

The 1910 Guerrero civil birth registration (src_002) was created at the time of the event by a civil registrar acting on the sworn appearance of the father, Sóstenes Cruz, fourteen days after the birth. The 1930 Mexico National Census (src_001) was enumerated twenty years later by a census enumerator who recorded an age stated by an unknown household respondent in Nueva Italia de Ruiz, Michoacán. Neither document derives from the other; they originate from different government systems (Guerrero civil registration vs. federal census), different dates (1910 vs. 1930), different places (Montes de Oca, Guerrero vs. Múgica, Michoacán), and different informants (father presenting before the civil registrar vs. an unknown household member responding to a census enumerator). There is no shared informant or shared underlying document. The two sources are independent for the purpose of this fact.
conflicts.weighing_analysis: Three factors decisively favor the civil birth registration. First, informant proximity: Sóstenes Cruz registered the birth in person just fourteen days after the event, making him a self-reporting, contemporaneous witness to a fact he personally experienced. The census respondent is unknown and spoke twenty years after the event from memory. Second, record purpose: the civil registration's sole purpose was to document the birth date — the fact in dispute — whereas the census used age to enumerate; an approximate age serves that purpose just as well as an exact one. Third, the discrepancy (four years) falls precisely within the well-documented range of Mexican census age rounding, where ages were commonly stated in round numbers or estimated from household members' approximate knowledge. The calendar check (convert_calendar, both dates) confirmed no calendar-system difference; the discrepancy is a genuine informant disagreement, with the census respondent the weaker informant.
conflicts.resolution_rationale:
The dispute is over Mauro Cruz Corona's birth year: the 1930 census implies approximately 1914, while the 1910 Guerrero civil birth registration states 22 November 1910. The four-year difference matters because the project objective placed his birth 'about 1910' and any proof conclusion for q_001 must account for the conflict.

The civil registration (a_079) records the birth date as 22 November 1910. The registrar based this on the sworn appearance of Sóstenes Cruz — the father — who presented the child before the civil authority fourteen days after the birth. This is a first-person, event-contemporaneous account entered into an official record whose explicit purpose was to document the precise date and place of birth.

The census entry (a_033) implies a birth year of approximately 1914 through a stated age (or age-derived calculation). The respondent is unknown — anyone in the household could have provided the age — and the information was given twenty years after the birth, from memory. The 1930 Mexico census is classified as indeterminate information quality throughout this project, reflecting that the informant's identity and proximity to the original event cannot be determined.

The civil registration is preferred on two grounds: the informant (the father) had direct, firsthand knowledge of the birth date; and the record was created within a fortnight of the event, before memory could degrade or rounding enter. The census error falls into the common historical pattern of age misreporting in Mexican censuses of this period, in which household ages were frequently rounded to the nearest five years or estimated by someone other than the person themselves — a well-documented pattern in Mexican civil registration research that routinely produces discrepancies of three to six years between census-derived birth years and contemporaneous registration records.

Browse-only Michoacán fallbacks (Apatzingán civil registro catalog, Apatzingán parish records) were appropriately set aside once the Guerrero birth record was found and verified as primary-quality and contemporaneous. The one collection not searched is Guerrero Catholic Church Records (collection 1823323, 1576–1979): a baptismal record would have been reported by the same informants (the parents) as the civil registration and cannot constitute a truly independent source under the evidence-independence rule; it also cannot plausibly contradict a primary-quality, contemporaneous civil registration made fourteen days after birth. The 1910 and 1921 Mexican census original household schedules are not publicly accessible — only compiled statistics survive. Research is declared exhaustive; all seven GPS stop criteria are met.
proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: Birth Date and Birth Place of Mauro Cruz Corona

**Research question:** What were the exact birth date and birth place of Mauro Cruz Corona, born about 1910 in or near Nueva Italia, Michoacán, Mexico?

**Conclusion:** Mauro Cruz Corona was born on 22 November 1910 in La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero, Mexico. The 1910 Guerrero civil birth registration establishes both facts with primary, contemporaneous evidence; the 1930 Mexico National Census independently corroborates his Guerrero origin. One conflict — a four-year discrepancy in birth year between the two sources — has been analyzed and resolved in favor of the civil registration. Research is declared exhaustive.

---

### Primary Evidence: 1910 Guerrero Civil Birth Registration

The authoritative basis for this conclusion is the civil birth registration of Mauro Cruz Corona, entered in the Guerrero civil registry on 6 December 1910 — fourteen days after the birth. The source is accessed through FamilySearch as: "México, Guerrero, Registro Civil, 1860-1996", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QGWQ-MCFV : accessed 5 October 2026), entry for Mauro Cruz Corona and Sóstenes Cruz, 6 de diciembre de 1910.

This record is an **original** source: it is the civil registration document itself, produced by a government registrar under statutory authority. The information concerning birth date and birth place is **primary**: it was supplied by Sóstenes Cruz, the father, who appeared in person before the civil registrar and personally declared the facts of his child's birth. The informant was a direct, eyewitness participant to the event. The registration occurred fourteen days after the birth — well within the normal timeliness of Mexican civil registration practice for this period — and before any degradation of memory could plausibly occur. This produces **direct** evidence bearing immediately on both the birth date and the birth place.

The registration records:
- **Birth date:** 22 November 1910 (exact; stated by father at registration)
- **Birth place:** La Unión, México — standardized as La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero, Mexico — consistent with the registration jurisdiction of Montes de Oca, Guerrero
- **Child's full name:** Mauro Cruz Corona (compound surname Cruz from father + Corona from mother)
- **Father:** Sóstenes Cruz (presenting informant)
- **Mother:** Apolinar Corona

The original image ARK is ark:/61903/3:1:33S7-9T8R-68V. The record content was supplied from the FamilySearch index/transcription; the image was not independently reviewed in this session. The mother's surname "Corona" appears as an OCR rendering in one index field; context and the alternate name field confirm "Corona." No discrepancy in the registrar's text itself has been identified.

This is the strongest available evidence class for a birth fact: original record, primary information, direct evidence, contemporaneous with the event.

---

### Corroborating Evidence: 1930 Mexico National Census

The 1930 Mexico National Census independently corroborates Mauro Cruz Corona's Guerrero origin. The census is accessed as: "México censo nacional, 1930," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MP5H-ZCT : accessed 2026-10-05), entry for Mauro Cruz in household of Feliciano Anguiano, Nueva Italia de Ruiz, Múgica, Michoacán, México, 1930; citing FamilySearch collection 1307314.

This source is a **derivative** — what was accessed is the FamilySearch indexed transcription of the 1930 Mexico National Census household schedule; the original schedule image (ark:/61903/3:1:S3HT-66R3-LH4) was identified but not independently reviewed. The information concerning birth state is **indeterminate**: the informant is an unknown household member who responded to the census enumerator, and the informant's identity and proximity to the original event cannot be determined. The evidence is **direct** as to birth state.

The census records:
- **Name:** Mauro Cruz (given name and paternal surname; maternal surname absent, as was common in census enumeration)
- **Birth year (derived):** approximately 1914
- **Birth state:** Guerrero (recorded as "Gerrero" — a phonetic variant spelling common in this period)
- **Residence in 1930:** Nueva Italia de Ruiz, Múgica, Michoacán, México

The census entry confirms that all five Cruz co-residents in the Anguiano household are recorded as born in Guerrero, including Mauro, his brothers, and his mother Apolinar Corona — establishing consistent family-level Guerrero origin independent of the civil registration.

---

### Resolution of Conflict c_001: Birth Year Discrepancy

The two sources disagree on birth year: the civil registration states 22 November 1910, while the 1930 census implies a birth year of approximately 1914 (derived from a stated or enumerated age). The four-year difference is the single conflict in this evidence set and has been resolved (c_001, status: resolved).

Three factors decisively favor the civil birth registration (a_079):

1. **Informant proximity.** Sóstenes Cruz registered the birth in person just fourteen days after the event. He was the child's father — a direct, firsthand participant. The census respondent is unknown; anyone in the Anguiano household could have provided the age, and the information was given from memory twenty years after the birth.

2. **Record purpose.** The civil registration's sole statutory purpose was to document the precise date and place of birth. An exact birth date is not incidental information — it is the document's reason for existing. A census age, by contrast, serves enumeration purposes; an approximate age answers that purpose just as well as a precise one, and census enumerators commonly accepted estimated ages.

3. **Documented census age-rounding pattern.** A four-year discrepancy falls precisely within the well-documented pattern of age misreporting in Mexican censuses of this period, in which household ages were frequently rounded to the nearest five years or estimated by someone other than the person themselves. This pattern routinely produces discrepancies of three to six years between census-derived birth years and contemporaneous registration records.

No calendar-system difference accounts for the discrepancy; both records use the Gregorian calendar. The census discrepancy is consistent with ordinary enumeration error in the 1930 Mexican census context and does not impugn the reliability of the civil registration.

---

### Geographic Finding

The project objective originally placed Mauro Cruz Corona's birth "in or near Nueva Italia, Michoacán, Mexico" — an assumption based on his 1930 residence, not a record-derived fact. The civil birth registration relocates the birth to Guerrero: La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero, Mexico. The 1930 census, from a fully independent institutional source, independently confirms Guerrero as his birth state. The siblings' civil birth registrations similarly record births in Guerrero municipalities (El Coco, La Unión, Guerrero for Miguel Cruz, 1913; Pochutla, Coahuayutla, Guerrero for Liborio Cruz, 1916; Rosario, Coahuayutla, Guerrero for Facundo Cruz, 1918). The family's Guerrero origins and subsequent migration to Michoacán (the 1930 residence) is consistent across multiple independent records.

---

### Research Scope

Michoacán indexed civil registro (FamilySearch collection 1916243) and Michoacán indexed Catholic church records (FamilySearch collection 1883388) were searched and returned no results for Mauro Cruz Corona — consistent with the family's Guerrero origin. The 1930 Mexico National Census (collection 1307314) was searched and located. The Guerrero indexed civil registration (collection 1918291) was searched, the index entry was located, and the original record was read (ARK ark:/61903/1:1:QGWQ-MCFV, log_007). The Guerrero Catholic Church Records (collection 1823323, 1576–1979) were not searched: a baptismal record for this event would have been reported by the same informants (the parents), cannot constitute a truly independent source under the evidence-independence rule, and cannot plausibly contradict a primary-quality, contemporaneous civil registration. The 1910 and 1921 Mexican census original household schedules are not publicly accessible. All seven GPS stop criteria were evaluated and met.

---

### Conclusion

The evidence proves that **Mauro Cruz Corona was born on 22 November 1910 in La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca, Guerrero, Mexico.** This conclusion rests on an original civil birth registration with primary information supplied by the child's father in person fourteen days after the birth, corroborated by an independent census source that confirms the birth state. The single conflict in the evidence — a four-year birth year discrepancy between the census and the civil registration — has been fully resolved in favor of the civil registration on grounds of informant proximity, record purpose, and well-documented census age-rounding patterns. Research is declared exhaustive. All five components of the Genealogical Proof Standard are met.

The Diocese of Michoacán was established in 1536 and became the Archdiocese of Michoacán in 1863. Church records for the Apatzingán / Tierra Caliente area fall under the Arquidiócesis de Morelia. Parish records must be searched at the parish level; diocesan-level documents (marriage dispensations, padrones parroquiales) are held at the Archivo Histórico of the Arquidiócesis de Morelia.

Women in Mexican civil and church records are recorded under their maiden surname, not their husband's. Searching for the mother's line requires knowing her maiden name (Corona or a variant).

The family shows mobility between Michoacán and adjacent Guerrero municipalities (siblings born in La Unión and Coahuayutla municipalities of Guerrero, 1913–1918). Search the Guerrero civil registration (FamilySearch collection 1918291, 1860–1996) for siblings and possibly parents. The adjoining Guerrero municipalities to the Apatzingán/Nueva Italia area include Coahuayutla de José María Izazaga and La Unión de Isidoro Montes de Oca.

The 1895 and 1900 national censuses exist only as compiled statistics; original household schedules were largely destroyed. Do not expect to find Mauro Cruz Corona's parents in a pre-1930 national census online.

All records are in Spanish. The civil registro de nacimiento entries use a formatted register style for the early 20th century. Use the FamilySearch Spanish Genealogical Word List and BYU Spanish Script Tutorial for reading handwritten entries.
localities.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Michoacán, Mexico — Apatzingán / Nueva Italia Area (1905–1920)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Michoacán became a Mexican state December 22, 1823 (5th state admitted). Apatzingán municipality created December 10, 1831. Nueva Italia de Ruiz founded 1909 as an agricultural colony.
- **Administrative center for the area:** Apatzingán de la Constitución (municipal seat)
- **Parent jurisdiction:** State of Michoacán, Mexico
- **Population during period:** Population data from the `place_population` tool was not returned for Michoacán at this query level. According to the FamilySearch Wiki, Michoacán is bordered by Jalisco, Guanajuato, Querétaro, State of Mexico, and Guerrero, with Pacific coastline to the southwest.
- **Economy:** Agricultural haciendas and colonias (Nueva Italia was founded as a commercial agricultural colony circa 1909 by Italian-descended investors); subsistence farming; cattle ranching throughout the Tierra Caliente and Tepalcatepec basin.
- **Ethnic composition:** Mestizo majority; Purépecha (Tarascan) indigenous minority in highland areas; small Italian-origin colonist presence in Nueva Italia post-1909.
- **Religious denominations:** Overwhelmingly Catholic. The Diocese of Michoacán was established 1536; it became the Archdiocese of Michoacán (Morelia) in 1863.
- **Key historical events:** Mexican Revolution (1910–1920) disrupted civil registration across much of Michoacán and Guerrero; hacienda and colonia labor unrest; Nueva Italia founded as a commercial agricultural colony ca. 1909.

## Boundary changes — CRITICAL FOR THIS RESEARCH

The municipality of Múgica (which today contains Nueva Italia de Ruiz) was **not created until February 12, 1942**. In 1905–1920, the territory of present-day Múgica — including Nueva Italia de Ruiz — was part of the **municipality of Apatzingán**.

All civil registration, church, and census records from 1905–1920 for Nueva Italia and its surroundings are therefore filed under **Apatzingán**, not Múgica. The FamilySearch Wiki for Múgica municipality ([https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/M%C3%BAgica,_Infiernillo,_Michoac%C3%A1n,_Mexico_Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/M%C3%BAgica,_Infiernillo,_Michoac%C3%A1n,_Mexico_Genealogy)) explicitly confirms there are no records available online for Múgica in civil registration, church, or census — because the pre-1942 records are under Apatzingán.

FamilySearch places Michoacán within the Infiernillo region for genealogical organization purposes; Apatzingán falls under the Tepalcatepec regional grouping.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Municipality level beginning 1859; Apatzingán civil registro runs 1867–1930 in the FamilySearch Catalog.
- **What exists:**
  - Births (nacimientos), marriages (matrimonios), and deaths (defunciones) for the municipality of Apatzingán, 1867–1930.
  - Digitized at FamilySearch Catalog: [Registros civiles del municipio de Apatzingán, 1867-1930](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/190084) — images available.
  - The statewide consolidated collection, [Mexico, Michoacán, Civil Registration, 1859-1940](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1916243) (FamilySearch collection 1916243), covers births, marriages, and deaths and is indexed with images. This is the primary searchable online source.
  - Ancestry hosts separate indexed + image collections: births 1859–1934 (Ancestry collection 60415), deaths 1859–1935 (60465), marriages 1859–1940 (60437).
- **Where held:** Physically: Michoacán Civil Registry State Archives (Morelia). Online: FamilySearch collection 1916243 and the Catalog entry above.
- **Content of birth records:** Date and time of birth; name and gender of child; parents' names, ages, civil status; paternal and maternal grandparents' names; birthplace. This is the single most important record for resolving both Mauro's birth date and his parents' identities.
- **Gaps:** Civil registration was not strictly enforced until 1867 and compliance remained uneven. The Mexican Revolution (1910–1920) disrupted record-keeping in many Michoacán municipalities. Births may have been registered late (months or even years after the event). The FamilySearch Wiki notes coverage at approximately 90–95 percent of the population for Michoacán overall, but rural and newly-settled areas like Nueva Italia likely had lower compliance.
- **Digitization level:** **Indexed + images** (FamilySearch collection 1916243; Ancestry collections 60415/60465/60437).

### Church records (Catholic baptismal registers)
- **Parish for Nueva Italia / Apatzingán area:** Iglesia Católica, Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, Apatzingán. This is the principal parish serving the Apatzingán municipality, which in 1905–1920 encompassed the Nueva Italia territory.
  - FamilySearch Catalog: [Nuestra Señora de la Asunción (Apatzingán, Michoacán) Parish Records, 1866-1967](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/320208) — images available.
  - Secondary: [Nuestra Señora de Acahuato (Acahuato, Michoacán) Parish Records, 1875-1925](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/1107030) — covers a neighboring area.
- **Diocesan archive:** Arquidiócesis de Morelia. Marriage dispensation documents and diocesan padrones are held at the Archivo Histórico of the Arquidiócesis de Morelia. The statewide collection [Mexico, Michoacan and Michoacan, Catholic Church Records, 1555-1996](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1883388) (FamilySearch collection 1883388) is indexed; coverage varies.
- **Content of baptismal records:** Date and place of baptism; infant's name and legitimacy status; parents' and godparents' names; sometimes grandparents' names and parents' residence.
- **Language:** Spanish.
- **Digitization level:** The Apatzingán parish record (Catalog 320208) is available as **browse-only images** — it must be browsed page by page with no name index at this level. Use the statewide collection 1883388 for a name search first; if a hit is found, then browse the original catalog images to confirm.
- **Note on Nueva Italia founding date:** Nueva Italia de Ruiz dates to approximately 1909. It had no dedicated parish church of its own in 1905–1920. Families in the area would have been served by the Apatzingán parish.

### Census records
- **1930 federal census (only publicly available federal census):**
  - [Mexico Census, 1930](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1307314) — indexed + images, free at FamilySearch. Also at Ancestry (collection 1771, subscription).
  - Municipality-level: [Censo de población del municipio de Apatzingán, Michoacán, 1930](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/668093) — images at FamilySearch Catalog.
  - The 1930 census records the household composition of all residents as of that year; Mauro Cruz Corona (age ~20 in 1930) would appear if he was still in the area, alongside siblings and potentially parents. It records birthplace, age, and marital status.
- **1910 and 1921 censuses:** The 1910 and 1921 national census original household schedules are not known to be publicly accessible online; according to the FamilySearch Wiki, the birthplace of those census records is not known, and generally only compiled statistics survive from pre-1930 enumerations. Do not expect to find Mauro's parents in a name-searchable 1910 census.
- **Parish padrones (ecclesiastical censuses):** [Padrones parroquiales: antigua Diócesis de Michoacán, 1734-1875](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/319912) — images at FamilySearch Catalog. These predate the 1905–1920 target period but may document earlier family presence in the region and grandparent-generation families.
- **Digitization level:** 1930 federal census — **indexed + images**. 1930 municipal census — **browse-only images**.

### Probate and court records
- Civil probate is administered at the municipality and state level. For the 1905–1920 period, probate records for Apatzingán would be held at the Apatzingán municipal courthouse and the state court archive in Morelia.
- Not currently available online for this municipality and period. Physical access or written inquiry required.

### Land records
- Mexico uses a mixed system of private titles, ejido grants, and hacienda records. The Apatzingán / Nueva Italia area was characterized by haciendas and colonias in 1905–1920.
- Notarial records (escrituras notariales) for land transactions are held at the Archivo de Notarías de Michoacán in Morelia and at local notary offices.
- The Archivo General de la Nación (AGN) in Mexico City holds land grant and hacienda records at the national level: [https://www.agn.gob.mx/](https://www.agn.gob.mx/).
- The FamilySearch Catalog lists [Mexico, Michoacán, Morelia, expedientes del gobierno y del ministerio de la hacienda, 1544-1896](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/1497849) — images.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Mexican Revolution 1910–1920.
- Service and pension records for the Revolution period are held at the Archivo Histórico de la SEDENA (Secretaría de la Defensa Nacional), Mexico City.
- The FamilySearch Wiki lists: [Dirección General de Archivo e Historia, SEDENA](https://www.gob.mx/sedena/acciones-y-programas/expedicion-de-documentos) for requesting military records.
- Not currently indexed online.

### Cemetery records
- The FamilySearch Wiki for Múgica municipality lists two cemeteries: **Panteón Ejidal de Gámbara** and **Panteón Municipal de Nueva Italia** (Calle Vicente Villada, Reforma, Múgica).
- Apatzingán has its own municipal cemetery: **Panteón Municipal de Apatzingán** (Avenida Corregidora, El Tarepe).
- Online coverage: FindAGrave and BillionGraves have some Mexican cemetery indexing but coverage for small Michoacán municipalities is sparse.

### Newspaper records
- Local newspapers for the Apatzingán / Tierra Caliente area in 1905–1920 are not known to be digitized. The state capital paper and regional press may be consulted at the Hemeroteca Nacional Digital de México ([http://www.hndm.unam.mx/](http://www.hndm.unam.mx/)).

### Immigration and emigration records
- **Border crossings to the US:** [Border Crossings: From Mexico to U.S., 1895-1964](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1082) at Ancestry (also FamilySearch collection 1803932, indexed, 1903–1957). Relevant if family members crossed into the US.
- Passenger lists and naturalization records: search NARA holdings and Ancestry.

### Other records
- **Valladolid Dispensas (marriage dispensations):** [https://www.valladoliddispensas.com/](https://www.valladoliddispensas.com/) — covers dispensas from the Diocesan Archive of Valladolid (Morelia) 1600–1899, useful for grandparent-generation marriages predating the target period.
- **Guerrero civil registration:** Because siblings of Mauro were born in Guerrero municipalities (La Unión and Coahuayutla) ca. 1913–1918, search [Mexico, Guerrero, Civil Registration, 1860-1996](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1918291) for siblings and potentially the parents' marriage record. The family was mobile across the Michoacán-Guerrero border.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Mexico, Michoacán, Civil Registration, 1859-1940 (collection 1916243, indexed + images); Mexico, Michoacan and Michoacan, Catholic Church Records, 1555-1996 (collection 1883388, indexed); Mexico Baptisms 1560-1950; Mexico Marriages 1570-1950; Mexico Deaths 1680-1940; Mexico Census 1930; FamilySearch Catalog images for Apatzingán civil registro (Catalog 190084) and parish (Catalog 320208) | Free |
| Ancestry | Michoacan, Mexico, Civil Registration Births, 1859-1934 (collection 60415); Deaths 1859-1935 (60465); Marriages 1859-1940 (60437); Michoacán, Mexico, Catholic Church Records, 1649-1909 (collection 60021); 1930 Mexico National Census (1771) | Subscription |
| MyHeritage | Mexico Baptisms, 1560-1950; Mexico Marriages, 1570-1950; Mexico Deaths, 1680-1940 | Subscription |
| Valladolid Dispensas | Marriage dispensations, Archdiocese of Morelia (Valladolid), 1600-1899 | Free |
| AGN (Archivo General de la Nación) | National-level land, colonial, and government records | In-person / online catalog |

**Coverage of this survey:** The volume_search returned 21,070 total digitized volumes matching Michoacán in the 1890–1930 range. The first two pages of results were examined (approximately 120 volumes). None of the first-page volumes cover Apatzingán specifically by name for birth/baptism records, though the parish at Tumbiscatío (96% indexed bautismos, 1894–1922, image group 004768410) and Villa Victoria/Chinicuila (97–98% indexed bautismos, 1892–1921, image groups 004768428/004768429) show the type of coverage that exists for nearby municipalities. The Apatzingán civil registro (Catalog 190084) and parish (Catalog 320208) are present as FamilySearch Catalog image sets but appear as browse-only rather than fully indexed volumes in the volume_search results examined.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Registro Civil del Estado de Michoacán (Morelia) | Original civil registration records; some can be ordered via [https://www.gob.mx/ActaNacimiento/](https://www.gob.mx/ActaNacimiento/) | In-person or online request |
| Archivo Histórico de la Arquidiócesis de Morelia | Diocesan church records, marriage dispensations, padrones parroquiales | In-person; contact the archdiocese |
| Archivo General del Estado de Michoacán (Morelia) | State government records, probate, land | In-person |

## Records NOT online

- Civil registration records for Apatzingán after 1930 (the FamilySearch collection ends at 1930/1940).
- Probate and court records for Apatzingán municipality, 1905–1920.
- Military Revolution-era service records for individuals from Michoacán.
- Most local newspaper archives for the Tierra Caliente / Apatzingán area, 1905–1920.
- Notarial / land records for Apatzingán haciendas and the Nueva Italia colonia establishment documents.
- Parish confirmation records (confirmaciones), which are a separate record type and were not consistently digitized.

## Known record losses

- The Mexican Revolution (1910–1920) disrupted civil registration across much of Michoacán. Some municipalities have gaps or missing volumes for years of peak conflict. The Apatzingán civil registro (1867–1930) appears intact in the FamilySearch Catalog, but specific years within that range should be verified by browsing the catalog entry.
- No courthouse fires or major specific record destructions for Apatzingán are documented in the FamilySearch Wiki, but this cannot be ruled out for the 1910–1920 decade.

## Research tips

- **Search Apatzingán, not Múgica.** The municipality of Múgica did not exist until 1942. All 1905–1920 records for Nueva Italia are filed under Apatzingán. The FamilySearch Wiki confirms there are no online records under Múgica at all. (Source: [Múgica, Infiernillo, Michoacán, Mexico Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/M%C3%BAgica,_Infiernillo,_Michoac%C3%A1n,_Mexico_Genealogy); [Apatzingán, Tepalcatepec, Michoacán, Mexico Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Apatzing%C3%A1n,_Tepalcatepec,_Michoac%C3%A1n,_Mexico_Genealogy))
- **Use both civil and church records simultaneously.** The FamilySearch Wiki for the Michoacán civil registration collection notes that civil registration covered about 90–95 percent of the population, but compliance was uneven in rural and newly-settled areas. The Apatzingán parish (Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, Catalog 320208) runs 1866–1967 and should be searched in parallel with the civil registro. (Source: [Mexico, Michoacan, Civil Registration - FamilySearch Historical Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico,_Michoacan,_Civil_Registration_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records))
- **Civil birth records name both parents and grandparents.** A Michoacán civil registro de nacimiento entry for ca. 1910 will typically include: the child's name, date/time/place of birth, father's full name and status, mother's full name (maiden surname) and status, paternal grandparents' names, and maternal grandparents' names. This single record can answer both research questions simultaneously. (Source: [Mexico Civil Registration](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Civil_Registration))
- **Compound surname structure:** Mauro Cruz Corona: 'Cruz' is the paternal first surname (father's paternal line); 'Corona' is the maternal first surname (mother's paternal line). His father's full surname would be Cruz [something] and his mother's full surname would be Corona [something]. (Source: [Mexico Naming Customs](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Naming_Customs))
- **Women keep their maiden name in all records.** Mauro's mother appears in records as [given name] Corona [second surname], not under any husband's name. Search for her under Corona. (Source: [Mexico Naming Customs](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Naming_Customs))
- **Search siblings' records to corroborate parents.** Birth records of Mauro's siblings (Miguel, Liborio, Facundo Cruz in Nueva Italia in the 1930 census) will name the same parents and may provide clearer or additional information. (Source: [Mexico Research Tips and Strategies](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Research_Tips_and_Strategies))
- **Cross the Guerrero border.** Siblings were born in La Unión and Coahuayutla municipalities of Guerrero (1913–1918). The family crossed the state line during the Revolution decade. Search [Mexico, Guerrero, Civil Registration, 1860-1996](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1918291) for siblings' birth records and the parents' marriage record, which may have occurred in Guerrero if the parents were residing there.
- **Search neighboring parishes.** If the Apatzingán parish has no entry, the FamilySearch Wiki recommends searching neighboring parishes. The parish at Acahuato (Catalog 1107030, 1875–1925) is the nearest secondary parish for the Apatzingán area.
- **The 1930 census is the strongest household substitute.** If Mauro or his parents were still in the Apatzingán area in 1930, the 1930 federal census and the Apatzingán municipal census (Catalog 668093) will show ages (and thus approximate birth years), birthplaces, and household relationships that can confirm or correct the ca. 1910 estimate. (Source: [Mexico Census](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Census))
- **Valladolid Dispensas for grandparent-generation.** If parents were married before 1900 and required a dispensation (e.g., for consanguinity), the [Valladolid Dispensas](https://www.valladoliddispensas.com/) index covers the Archdiocese of Morelia 1600–1899 and is free to search online. These dispensas often contain genealogical detail going back several generations.
- **All records are in Spanish.** Use the [Spanish Genealogical Word List](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Spanish_Genealogical_Word_List) and the [BYU Spanish Script Tutorial](https://script.byu.edu/spanish-handwriting/introduction) for reading handwritten entries from this period.
